title: Evaluation of Dynamic Cointegration-Based Pairs Trading Strategy in the Cryptocurrency Market

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper implements a dynamic cointegration-based pairs trading strategy in the cryptocurrency market using three different scenarios. In the formation period, the Engle-Granger methodology, Kapetanios-Snell-Shin (KSS) test, and Johansen test are used to test for linear and nonlinear cointegration. The mean-reversion speed of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process is calibrated to obtain the half-life, which determines the look-back window for computing Z-scores, and trading signals are generated when spreads diverge by two standard deviations and closed when they converge within one standard deviation.
extraction.universe: Cryptocurrency contracts on the BitMEX exchange including perpetual swaps and futures

key_findings: A basket pairs trading strategy using a dynamic Johansen cointegration test improves risk-adjusted profitability, achieving a Sharpe ratio of 7.94.
The dynamic pairs trading strategy consistently outperforms the naive buy-and-hold strategy across the BitMEX exchange.
Certain coins such as Tron (TRX), Cardano (ADA), and Ripple (XRP) exhibit better statistical arbitrage opportunities and higher performance across various scenarios.
Incorporating market microstructure constraints such as order execution based on available volume makes the backtesting much more realistic.
limitations: Increasing the number of coins and diversification lowers trading risk but also decreases the strategy's return.
Market jumps can cause non-proper signals in the strategy.
